title: Key Vault Secrets, Keys, and Certificates
description: Dive into the three main object types in Key Vault and learn when to use each one.

data.text: Each object type in Key Vault serves a distinct purpose. Secrets store plain-text values. Keys perform cryptographic operations. Certificates are keys wrapped in a certificate lifecycle, including issuance and renewal.

cards.title: Secrets
cards.description: Opaque values up to 25 KB each. Best for API keys, connection strings, and passwords.
cons: Stored as plain text inside the vault

cards.title: Keys
cards.description: Cryptographic keys for encryption, decryption, and signing.

cards.title: Certificates
cards.description: TLS/SSL or code-signing certificates with auto-renewal.

data.title: Store and Retrieve a Secret
data.content: Add a connection string to Key Vault and read it back with the Azure CLI.
data.code:
# Store a secret
az keyvault secret set   --vault-name myKeyVault   --name "DefaultConnection"   --value "Server=tcp:my-sql.database.windows.net;..."

# Retrieve a secret
az keyvault secret show   --vault-name myKeyVault   --name "DefaultConnection"   --query value -o tsv

data.title: Create an RSA Key
data.content: Provision an RSA key for signing or encryption.
data.code: az keyvault key create   --vault-name myKeyVault   --name "my-signing-key"   --kty RSA   --size 2048   --ops sign verify encrypt decrypt

data.text: Every secret, key, and certificate has a name and one or more versions. Writing a new value to the same name creates a new version; the old version remains available and can still be read by version ID. Applications that reference a secret without a version get the latest enabled version, which is what makes rotation possible without redeploying. To rotate safely, create the new version, let consumers pick it up, then disable the old version after a grace period.

data.title: Rotate a secret without downtime
data.content: Create a new version, verify consumers read it, then disable the previous version. Audit the version history to confirm.
data.code:
# Create a new version of the same secret name
az keyvault secret set --vault-name shop-kv --name SqlPassword --value "N3wS3cure!"

# List versions, newest first
az keyvault secret list-versions --vault-name shop-kv --name SqlPassword \
  --query "[].{id:id, enabled:attributes.enabled, created:attributes.created}" -o table

# Disable the old version once consumers have refreshed
az keyvault secret set-attributes --vault-name shop-kv --name SqlPassword \
  --version "<old-version-id>" --enabled false

data.title: Create a certificate with an issuance policy
data.content: A Key Vault certificate bundles a key, a secret, and the certificate lifecycle. The policy controls issuer, subject, key type, and renewal.
data.code:
az keyvault certificate create \
  --vault-name shop-kv \
  --name shop-tls \
  --policy @cert-policy.json

# cert-policy.json (excerpt)
# {
#   "issuerParameters": { "name": "Self" },
#   "x509CertificateProperties": {
#     "subject": "CN=shop.example.com",
#     "subjectAlternativeNames": { "dnsNames": ["shop.example.com"] },
#     "validityInMonths": 12
#   },
#   "keyProperties": { "keyType": "RSA", "keySize": 2048, "reuseKey": false }
# }

rows: RSA or EC key material and operations

data.title: Deleting a secret deletes every version
data.text: There is no per-version delete that preserves the name. If you need to retire a value, disable it and keep the history for audit. Deleting the whole secret is a recovery event, not a rotation step.

data.title: Work with Key Vault Objects
data.description: Create a Key Vault, store a secret, generate a key, and verify the objects exist.
steps: Set a secret named 'ApiKey' with value 'secret-123'.
List all secrets and keys to verify they exist.
data.expectedOutcome: You see the secret and key in the Key Vault and can retrieve their values.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Use secrets for simple values like passwords and connection strings.
Use keys when you need encryption or signing.
Use certificates when you need TLS or auto-renewal.
data.takeaway: Key Vault is not just a safe for passwords — it is your app's cryptographic backbone.
